title: Casimir endomorphism and trace for a semisimple algebraic group
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A rational module for an affine finite-type $F$-group scheme $G$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] means an $F$-vector space $V$ with a coaction $V\to V\otimes_F F[G]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity. A submodule is a subspace whose coaction takes values in its tensor product with $F[G]$. A simple module is nonzero and has no proper nonzero submodule. An equivariant linear map means one commuting with coactions, equivalently with the actions after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Assume $G$ is smooth and connected [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme] and semisimple: it has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup, where solvable means its successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Let $V$ be finite-dimensional, let $\mathfrak g=T_eG$ be the tangent space at the identity [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], write $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ for the action morphism, and let $d r:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ be the differential of its action. On dual-number points [def-sc-dual-numbers] this is specified by $r(1+\epsilon x)=1+\epsilon d r(x)$. Put $\mathfrak h=d r(\mathfrak g)\subseteq\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ and $n=\dim_F\mathfrak h$. The trace form $B(X,Y)=\operatorname{Tr}_V(XY)$ on $\mathfrak h$ is nondegenerate. For any basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $\mathfrak h$ and its $B$-dual basis $e^1,\ldots,e^n$, the actual endomorphism
$$c_V=\sum_{i=1}^n e_i e^i\in\operatorname{End}_F(V)$$
is independent of that basis, is $G$-equivariant, and satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}_V(c_V)=n\cdot1_F$. If the action on $V$ is nontrivial (its coaction is not $v\mapsto v\otimes1$), then $n>0$. For every rational submodule $W\subseteq V$, $c_V(W)\subseteq W$; if the induced action on $V/W$ is trivial, then $c_V(V)\subseteq W$. Empty bases give $c_V=0$ when $\mathfrak h=0$.

source.place: Section 22c, The Casimir operator, printed pp.475-476; Proposition 22.41, printed p.477, for the nonzero differential image and trivial-quotient properties; Proposition 10.31, printed p.196, for differentiation and stabilizers.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-char-zero-differentiation-hom], $dr$ is a Lie homomorphism from the finite-dimensional tangent Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. By [lem-sfb-char-zero-semisimple-group-lie], $\mathfrak g$ is semisimple. The corestriction $dr:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak h$ is surjective by the definition of $\mathfrak h$ as its image. Apply [lem-sfb-semisimple-lie-surjective-image] to obtain semisimplicity of $\mathfrak h$. Its inclusion in $\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ is an injective Lie representation. Therefore [lem-sfb-faithful-semisimple-trace-form] gives exactly the required nondegeneracy of $B$.

source.place: §22c, printed pp.475-476, faithful trace form and passage to the differential image.

proof.text:
Choose a basis $(e_i)$ of $\mathfrak h$. The matrix $(B(e_i,e_j))$ is invertible by nondegeneracy, so its inverse gives the unique dual basis $(e^i)$ with $B(e_i,e^j)=\delta_i^j$. If $f_j=\sum_i e_i A_{ij}$ is another basis, its dual is $f^j=\sum_k(A^{-1})_{jk}e^k$. Hence
$$\sum_j f_j f^j=\sum_{i,k,j}A_{ij}(A^{-1})_{jk}e_i e^k=\sum_i e_i e^i.$$
Thus the displayed actual endomorphism is independent of the choice of basis; the calculation uses only bilinearity and $AA^{-1}=I$.

source.place: §22c, printed p.475, definition and basis independence of the Casimir operator (change-of-basis calculation expanded).

proof.text:
For $X,Y,Z\in\mathfrak h$, cyclicity of matrix trace gives
$$B([X,Y],Z)+B(Y,[X,Z])=\operatorname{Tr}(XYZ-YZX)=0.$$
Write $[X,e_i]=\sum_j a_{ji}e_j$. Pairing $[X,e^i]$ with $e_j$ then gives $[X,e^i]=-\sum_j a_{ij}e^j$. Expanding commutators with products yields
$$[X,c_V]=\sum_{i,j}a_{ji}e_j e^i-\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}e_i e^j=0,$$
by exchanging $i,j$. Thus $c_V$ commutes with every $dr(x)$. The morphism criterion in [lem-sfb-char-zero-differentiation-hom], applied to $u=c_V:M=V\to N=V$, proves rational $G$-equivariance, including every algebra extension.

source.place: §22c, printed pp.475-476, Lie commutation and G-equivariance; Proposition 10.31 (graph-stabilizer criterion).

proof.text: Trace is linear, and every summand has trace $\operatorname{Tr}_V(e_i e^i)=B(e_i,e^i)=1_F$. Consequently $\operatorname{Tr}_V(c_V)=\sum_{i=1}^n1_F=n\cdot1_F$. For $n=0$ the only basis is empty and its sum is the zero endomorphism, with trace zero; nondegeneracy on the zero space is vacuous.

If $n=0$, then $dr=0$. Give the same vector space $V$ its trivial rational action, denoted $V_{\rm triv}$, whose differential is zero by the dual-number formula. The linear identity $u:V_{\rm triv}\to V$ intertwines the two differentials. By [lem-sfb-char-zero-differentiation-hom] it intertwines their coactions, so the original coaction on $V$ is $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. Contrapositively, a nontrivial action has $n>0$.

source.place: Proposition 22.41, printed p.477, assertion that a nontrivial action has nonzero differential image; Proposition 10.31 with graph stabilizers.

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq V$ be a rational submodule. Evaluate its action after scalar extension to $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. For $w\in W$ and $x\in\mathfrak g$, the vector $(1+\epsilon dr(x))w$ lies in $W\otimes_F F[\epsilon]$, hence its coefficient $dr(x)w$ of $\epsilon$ lies in $W$. Thus every $e_i$ and $e^i$ preserves $W$, and so does their sum of products $c_V$. If the quotient action on $V/W$ is trivial, reducing $(1+\epsilon dr(x))v$ modulo $W\otimes_F F[\epsilon]$ gives $dr(x)v\in W$. Then $e^i(V)\subseteq W$ and $e_i(W)\subseteq W$, whence every $e_i e^i(V)\subseteq W$ and $c_V(V)\subseteq W$. This also holds for the empty sum.
